headline: Deliberate practice is focused improvement—working on weaknesses with feedback, not just repetition
universal_truth: Improvement requires intention; doing something repeatedly doesn't mean doing it better
fun_facts: Expert performers in most fields have accumulated about 10,000 hours of deliberate practice
Deliberate practice feels effortful—if it's comfortable, you're not in the learning zone
Feedback within seconds leads to 3x faster improvement than delayed feedback
discussion_questions: When do you practice deliberately versus just go through motions?
What skill would improve most from focused, intentional work?
How do you get feedback on your weaknesses?

hook.script: Playing guitar for 20 years doesn't make you a master—practicing deliberately does. Deliberate practice targets weaknesses, seeks feedback, and pushes past comfort. Repetition without intention is just motion.

cliff.script: We often confuse activity with improvement. What's the difference between practice and deliberate practice?

options.text: Deliberate practice targets specific weaknesses with immediate feedback—it's uncomfortable because you're working at the edge of your ability, not reinforcing what you already know
options.response: Yes. Comfort means you're not learning. Deliberate practice is effortful, focused, and targeted at weaknesses. That's what builds skill. Easy practice just maintains.

options.text: More practice hours lead to more skill
options.response: Hours matter, but quality matters more—10 focused hours beat 100 unfocused ones...

fact1.title: Comfort Zone vs Learning Zone
fact1.script: In the comfort zone, you're not learning—just reinforcing. In the learning zone, you're slightly beyond current ability. That's where growth happens. Deliberate practice keeps you in the learning zone.

fact2.title: Feedback Loop
fact2.script: Without feedback, you can't correct. Deliberate practice includes immediate feedback so errors become adjustments. The faster the feedback, the faster the improvement.

fact3.title: Target Weaknesses
fact3.script: It's fun to practice what you're good at. Deliberate practice targets what you're bad at. That's uncomfortable but effective. Skill gaps don't close without focused attention.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Improvement requires intention. Doing something repeatedly doesn't mean doing it better. Practice deliberately.

outro.script: That's Day 285. Tomorrow, we'll explore when practice becomes skill—mastery. Until then, identify where you could practice more deliberately.

growTrack.title: Deliberate Practice Plan - What Needs Focused Work?
growTrack.learning_objective: Design deliberate practice for skill improvement
growTrack.activity: Choose a skill you want to improve. What specifically is weak? How can you get immediate feedback? Design a 30-minute deliberate practice session targeting your specific weaknesses.
